Platform Migration Report

Prepared for the engineering leadership review, this report summarizes the outcome of the Q3 infrastructure migration and what it means for upcoming releases.

Background

The legacy system had accumulated years of technical debt, and on-call load had grown steadily uncomfortable. The migration was scoped to reduce incident volume & simplify deploys.

Outcomes

The team’s velocity improved after the migration. Deploy frequency roughly doubled, and the median time to recover from an incident dropped from forty minutes to under nine.

Every workstream was validated against its own acceptance criteria before rollout, and no workstream shipped without sign-off from at least two reviewers.

“We haven’t had a Sev-1 in six weeks — that hasn’t happened since before the rewrite.” — on-call lead

Risks & Follow-ups

A few items remain open. The billing service still depends on the old queue, and its own acceptance criteria have not yet been finalized with the finance team.

  • Finish decommissioning the legacy queue consumers
  • Backfill integration tests for the billing edge cases
  • Document the new on-call runbook

Next Steps

The following sequence is proposed for the next two sprints:

  1. Freeze the legacy write path
  2. Migrate remaining billing consumers
  3. Retire the old cluster
